prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1133; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a side impact at a signalized intersection, with the insured vehicle struck on the driver side by a vehicle entering from the cross street. The claimant reports neck pain and has retained counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it and that coverage was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained the statements of the other driver and two independent witnesses, all of whom describe the collision the same way. Scene photos are consistent with that account.

Entry 4: Inspected the vehicle. The damage is mostly in line with the described impact, concentrated on the driver-side door and quarter panel, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the repair history.

Entry 5: Medical records show a whiplash diagnosis, which is a plausible injury for a crash of this type. No earlier injury to the same area is known from the records obtained so far.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a usual course, with physical therapy and medication, and the claimant's symptoms tapered as they improved. Follow-up visits have become less frequent.

Entry 7: In a recorded interview the claimant added some small details about the sequence of events, but the core account has not changed. It is still unclear from the statements where in the vehicle the claimant was seated at impact, and I have asked counsel to clarify.

Entry 8: Based on the evidence reviewed so far, the claim is consistent with the reported loss and injury. Continuing to monitor the treatment record and will request a final medical summary before setting a settlement range.
